outcome.technical: NO CODE CHANGED. The task asks for a tool that already exists: tools/measure-affected-miss.py (1254 lines) was committed by P131.16-dau (b52ba79a, identical title) and amended by P132.5-5mm (66b3635d). It carries its own 21-case suite (python3 tools/measure-affected-miss.py --selftest: ALL PASS 21/21, exit 0). Acceptance (1) is m6 (miss counted AND named on a fixture repo, 'misses 1 of 1 commits (mutation)'), (2) is m8 (selection holding every red suite -> 'misses 0 of 1', raise mutation did turn 2 suites red), (3) is m10 (no gh on PATH -> asked False, 'could-not-ask' shown, 'runs (CI)' absent), (4) is m13 (git status --porcelain, worktree list, HEAD and scratch dirs equal before/after a run). Scope notes: (a) I did NOT create tests/test_measure_affected_miss.py: tools/*.py keep an in-module --selftest by design - tools/sweep-selftests.py SWEEP_DIRS = tests, tools, .claude/hooks and runs `<tool> --selftest` for every tool (its comment: every tool suite runs HERE); only plugin hooks/ and scripts/ owe a suite in tests/. selftest_coverage() walks only tools/lints, tools/demo and two benches (164 total, 0 uncovered/exempt/stale/orphans); tools/measure-affected-miss.py is outside its walk, as every other tools/*.py is, and is held by the sweep instead. A second copy of the cases in tests/ would be a duplicate. (b) tools/affected.py and CONTRIBUTING.md need no change: affected.py's docstring already points at this tool, CONTRIBUTING.md:507 already documents it, and PROSE_SCAN_EXEMPT in tools/lints/_output_lints.py already carries the tool's row. Dependants answered: tests/test__output_lints.py (path refs at :1677,:1684) still correct, the file is unchanged; tools/affected.py still correct (docstring pointer); tools/lints/_output_lints.py still correct (exemption row); CONTRIBUTING.md still correct (paragraph at :507 describes the tool as it is). (c) Acceptance (5), small window, run once: `python3 tools/measure-affected-miss.py --commits 2 --budget-minutes 40 --timeout 1200 --ci-limit 6 --sweep-cmd "python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --quiet --jobs 4"` from the P142.3 tree (window ad586f07b..d33730d60), exit 0, output: '[1/2] d33730d60 feat(P141.1)...: NOT MEASURED - style: sweep exit None said: timed out after 1200s' ; '[2/2] ad586f07b feat(P140.2-ohy)...: the selection was the full set, so no suite can be missed' ; 'window: 2 task commit(s), ad586f07b..d33730d60, 1 measured (1 of them the full set, which cannot miss)' ; 'misses 0 of 1 commits (mutation); 0 of 1 runs (CI)'. End to end the tool ran both halves, removed its scratch worktrees (git worktree list holds none, TMPDIR holds no measure-affected-miss-* dir after the run) and left the checkout status unchanged; but the one measured commit was a full-set selection, so that run is ZERO evidence about the miss rate, and the other commit hit the sweep timeout on a machine shared with two other executors. The real gh was probed once first: `gh run list --status failure --limit 2 --json databaseId,headSha,createdAt,workflowName` returns a JSON list of those four keys, exactly what ci_half() parses. The 20-commit command for the orchestrator, on a quiet machine, from the project dir: `python3 tools/measure-affected-miss.py --commits 20 --budget-minutes 240 --timeout 2400 --ci-limit 30 --json > <file>` (default sweep command; a mutation sweep per changed .py per commit took over 20 minutes under load here and 7-12 minutes in P131.16, so budget hours; --budget-minutes stops starting commits past it and says so). Alternatives: --no-ci for the mutation half alone, --ci-only --ci-since <date> for the CI half alone.
